doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Playing with Nicki Parrott; desert island records
summary: She no longer thinks about gender when picking players, loves playing with Nicki, and names Buddy Rich, Mel Lewis, Ray Brown and others for her five CDs.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Let me ask you the question about you’re on a desert island and you can take five CDs or LPs.

Okay. Well see I’ll tell you that in a second. But what I was going to tell you, I’m sorry I got off my track with the not hiring women and stuff. But now like with Diva and Five Play, I don’t know if it’s the people, because I work with them all the time anyway, but like our bass player, I used to have this incredible fantasy. I always wanted to play a shuffle with Ray Brown. It’s like I love Ray Brown. But now I mean I love playing with Nicki. I think she’s one of the best bass players I know. And now it just becomes a matter of, you know there’s just certain players, it doesn’t matter that Nicki is a woman or a man or whatever she is, she’s just my favorite, like one of my absolute favorite bass players. So now you have wider choices. And for me it’s kind of neat because I don’t have to think oh, the women thing again. Because it never, never occurs to me. Like it never occurred to me before to hire a woman. Now it never occurs to me to worry like, oh, should I hire a man, should I hire a woman. I mean I never think of that. I just think who do I like. And I’m lucky now that I’m not so, I’m much more enlightened than I was. Okay so my five CDs. I would take a Buddy Rich compilation CD or his “Big Swing Face” album which I love, I would take one of my Mel Lewis albums — I’d have to think about which one to take, probably the one with “Groove Merchant” on it. Mel Lewis. I’d probably take — I can’t tell you this, I have to wittle down my list, but I’d take a Ray Brown trio album with Jeff Hamilton and Gene Harris on it. Probably an Oscar Peterson trio album, and maybe probably a Frank Sinatra record or Ella Fitzgerald. I don’t know. I need more time to prepare.
